narrative:
Your loan application was reviewed and, based on an automated assessment of your financial profile, the system determined there is a 59% likelihood that you represent a credit risk — a probability just above the threshold that led to your application being denied. While this is not an overwhelming margin, it was enough to result in a rejection, and understanding the specific reasons behind this outcome may help you take steps to improve your situation.

The most influential factor in this decision was the status of your checking account, which currently holds between 0 and 200 Deutsche Marks. Among applicants who were approved, the largest group — about half — had no checking account at all, while yours falls into a range that the model associates with financial instability. A low checking account balance can signal limited financial cushion, and in your case, this was the single strongest driver pushing the assessment toward a higher credit risk.

Interestingly, your credit history actually worked in your favor. Having a "critical or other credits" history might sound concerning, but this category is quite common among approved applicants — roughly 35% of those who were approved share this same credit history profile. This factor pulled the prediction in a positive direction, partially offsetting some of the other concerns.

However, the fact that you currently have an active installment plan through a bank was the third most important factor, and it pushed the assessment further toward risk. Having an existing bank installment plan on top of a new loan request raises concerns about your overall debt load, and only about 12% of approved applicants were in a similar situation — the vast majority had no other installment plans at all.

Beyond these top three factors, a few other aspects of your profile are worth noting. You are requesting a loan over 24 months, which is longer than the average of about 19 months among approved applicants, and your installment rate of 4% of disposable income is higher than the approved average of roughly 3%, meaning repayments would take a larger share of your budget. You also have 2 existing credits at this bank, compared to an average of about 1.4 among approved applicants, and you support 2 financially dependent people, above the average of around 1.1 — both of which add to the picture of financial pressure.

To improve your chances in the future, consider building up your checking account balance before reapplying, as a stronger financial buffer could significantly change how your application is assessed. Paying off or completing your existing bank installment plan before applying again would also remove one of the key risk signals. Finally, if possible, applying for a shorter loan duration or a lower installment rate could further strengthen your profile and bring it closer in line with applicants who are typically approved.
